doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

chapter: The trombone and the business today
title: Keeping the trombone alive and the start of Hip-Bone Music
summary: Davis recalls his first Hip-Bone record with sixteen New York trombonists and praises younger players.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Do you feel driven to help in any way you can to keep the trombone alive?

For sure. That’s why this was years — actually this is our 30 anniversary of Hip-Bone Music when I started. And the first record that I did was with the 16 different trombone players from New York, although Watrous was in town so we got him to play on two of the tracks. He was the only guy that wasn’t a New York-based person. But people like Steve Turré, Robin Eubanks, Conrad Herwig, Birch Johnson, Jim Pugh played on that, Dave Taylor. And a lot of that was, yeah, for what you’re just describing Monk, like trying to highlight the instrument for what it can do. And I certainly still subscribe to that a hundred percent. It’s a lot easier now because of all these phenomenal younger players like Marshall and Mike Dease and Ryan Keberle who are just taking the instrument and running with it, so it’s in really good hands. So I think the work that those gentlemen — and many others too — I’m leaving people out that I shouldn’t be leaving out. But it’s very healthy right now so I feel — I think the trombone is in good shape for decades to come.
